{"content": "### Install a tool using uv tool install

Source: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/docs/guides/tools.md

Installs a specified tool, like Ruff, to a persistent environment, making its executables available in the system's PATH.

```console
$ uv tool install ruff
```

--------------------------------

### Install command-line tools with uv tool

Source: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/docs/guides/integration/docker.md

Ensures the tool executable path is present in PATH and installs executable tools using uv tool.

```dockerfile
ENV PATH=/root/.local/bin:$PATH
RUN uv tool install cowsay
```

--------------------------------

### Install a package from a local disk path with uv pip

Source: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/docs/pip/packages.md

Installs a Python package directly from a local directory or archive on the disk.

```console
$ uv pip install "ruff @ ./projects/ruff"
```

--------------------------------

### Configure custom uv tool binary directory

Source: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/docs/guides/integration/docker.md

Sets the UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR environment variable to override the default location where tool executables are placed.

```dockerfile
ENV UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR=/opt/uv-bin/
```

### Installing tools

Source: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/docs/guides/tools.md

When a tool is installed, its executables are placed in a `bin` directory within the `PATH`, allowing the tool to be run directly without `uv`. If the tool is not on the `PATH`, a warning will be displayed, and `uv tool update-shell` can be used to add it.", "results": []}
